label: Ubiquiti UniFi Mobile Router (UMR)
description: UniFi Mobile Router: 2x 1G RJ45, LTE Cat 4 (150/50 Mbps), WiFi 4, PoE+ input with 10 W PoE passthrough, DIN/wall mount.
notes: Vendor figures: **(2) GbE RJ45 ports**, **LTE Cat 4** (150 Mbps down / 50 Mbps up), WiFi 4 1x1, 9 W, PoE+ (48-54 V) or USB-C or 4-pin ATX DC. The PoE row is the interesting one: **(1) PoE input and (1) PoE output, max 10 W, which requires a PoE+ switch** - so it can be powered by the switch it sits on *and* pass power through to one downstream device, but only when the upstream is PoE+ rather than plain 802.3af. **Cited 2026-11-19.** Port row, 9 W draw and the PoE classes: https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/integrations/umr-us (200, 708,698 B) prints "Networking Interface (2) GbE RJ45 ports, LTE Cat 4 radio, WiFi 4", "PoE Interface (1) PoE input / (1) PoE output (Max. 10W, requires PoE+ switch)", "Max. Power Consumption 9W" and "Power Method PoE+ (48-54V DC)". Datasheet https://dl.ui.com/ds/umr_ds.pdf (200, application/pdf, 597,924 B, two pages, text layer) prints the same census as "(2) GbE RJ45 ports" and "(1) PoE in / (1) PoE output*" with "*Requires a PoE+ switch" - but no output wattage, so the 10 W budget is a tech-spec-only figure. The store page https://store.ui.com/us/en/products/umr-us (307 to its collection URL, 200 there at 585,616 B) corroborates it in prose: "PoE+ input required for PoE passthrough." The two documents disagree on the chassis - datasheet 220.6 x 89.8 x 28.8 mm and 252/298 g against tech-spec 190 x 89.8 x 28.8 mm and 257/303 g - while the ports, the 150 Mbps WiFi 4 rate and the 9 W draw are identical on both, and those are what the row models. Neither surface publishes *which* RJ45 is the input, only that there is one of each, so rj45-1 sinks (9 W) and rj45-2 sources (PoE+), the same convention as devices/zyxel/gs1900-24ep.json. The -us suffix is required on both hosts: store /products/umr is 404 and techspecs .../integrations/umr lands on the 609,911-byte front page.

poe.note: (1) PoE output, max 10 W, and it requires a PoE+ switch upstream - so the passthrough is bounded at 10 W on the one PSE port (rj45-2). The 10 W is printed only by the tech-spec page; the datasheet states the port count and the PoE+ upstream requirement but no output wattage.
